bullets.title: AI sentiment rout: SOX -11.4% in worst semi streak since 2006
bullets.body: The semiconductor sector logged eight consecutive losing sessions (longest since May 2006), with SOX down ~11.4% for the week and the AI Tech Beneficiaries basket (MSXXAIB) falling -16.5% WoW—its worst week since inception in early 2023. The selloff was triggered by CoreWeave debt stress (CDS spiking to ~1,194bp, implying >60% default probability), Gartner's warning that $3.5T of AI infrastructure spending is at impairment risk by 2030, and Anthropic revenue growth slowing to 43% YoY. Net tech selling reached ~$10B over 6 sessions, the largest since DeepSeek in Jan 2025.

bullets.title: AI credit bifurcation: hyperscalers resilient, neoclouds distressed
bullets.body: USD HY AI-related corporates and data-center project finance are under the most pressure, while IG hyperscalers remain relatively stable. CoreWeave unsecured bonds traded below 80¢ at ~15% yields; ORCL credit also widening. Goldman, JPM, and Morgan Stanley all frame this as a reassessment of AI capex economics and financing costs—not broad credit deterioration. GS sees USD HY AI-related spreads as having near-term reversal scope but maintains underweight IG Tech.

bullets.title: September CPI/PPI hotter than expected; October hike odds volatile
bullets.body: September core CPI printed 0.33% m/m (vs 0.2% consensus), driving October hike odds as high as ~50% before Warsh's noncommittal IMF remarks pulled them back to ~15-16%. Core PPI came in at +0.7% m/m vs +0.3% consensus. Multiple banks and strategists converge on Fed holding in October, hiking in December, with March 2027 as the next step. Core PCE September is tracking ~0.32-0.34% m/m with the 3-month annualized pace rising to ~2.7-2.8%.

bullets.title: Sticky inflation regime: Hedgeye nowcast +3.88%; no disinflationary scenarios remain
bullets.body: Hedgeye's October CPI nowcast is +3.88% y/y (+14bp acceleration from prior estimate), with the monthly model showing 90% directional accuracy. JPMorgan's global data watch flags global core goods CPI accelerating to 2.5%ar this quarter, roughly double the prior year pace, with services inflation above 3.5%ar in the US and Euro area. AI-driven demand is increasingly cited as a source of goods-price stickiness alongside energy and tariffs.

bullets.title: Fed likely holds October, hikes December and March; rates curve dynamics key
bullets.body: Broad consensus across JPM, Morgan Stanley, Piper Sandler, and others: October skip is near-certain, December hike is the strong base case, and March 2027 is a live meeting. Market is pricing ~27bp of hikes through year-end with 90%+ probability of a December move. JPM recommends 10s/30s steepeners as low-beta long exposure; 30-year bond target yield floor at 5.15-5.25% in Q4.

bullets.title: Macro data strong: IP surged to 49-month high; retail sales +6.8% YoY
bullets.body: September industrial production rose +0.7% m/m (vs +0.4% estimate), the highest level since Dec 2018, with High-Tech Industries +1.49% m/m and +17.6% YoY. Retail sales accelerated to +6.8% YoY in September (vs +4.9% August). Consumer credit card spending from JPM/WFC/Citi running +10-11% YoY. Despite this, real hourly earnings are negative for 3 consecutive months as inflation exceeds wage growth.

bullets.title: Hyperscaler capex raised again: $818B in CY26, $1.17T in CY27
bullets.body: JPM raised cloud DC capex to +85% growth in 2026 (~$270B+ dollar increase) and +70% in 2027 (~$400B+). Morgan Stanley raised its AI capex estimate ~14% to $1.6T in 2027. Jefferies models CY26 at ~$818B (+84%) and CY27 at ~$1.17T (+43%). AI-related capex is expected to drive ~25% of SPX sales growth in 2027 and accounts for >60% of SPX+select neocloud capex.

bullets.title: TSMC raises FY26 revenue guide to +44%; N2 capacity to more than double in 2027
bullets.body: TSMC reported Q3 revenue of $46.7B (beating $45.4B consensus) and guided Q4 to $53.3B vs. $50.1B consensus, raising FY26 growth to +44% (vs prior +40%) on robust AI/HPC demand with no signs of slowdown. N2 accounted for ~8% of quarterly wafer revenue and capacity is expected to more than double in CY27. Management is evaluating Texas Terafab expansion with SpaceX but insists TSMC must operate any such facility. FY26-28 capex will be significantly higher than the prior three years; JPM raised its 2027 capex estimate to $83B.

bullets.title: Hedge fund AI exposure reversal: largest net selling on record in Info Tech
bullets.body: Goldman Sachs Prime reports Info Tech was the most net-sold global sector with the largest percentage net selling on record (since 2016). All cumulative hedge-fund net buying in Global AI since start of 2025 has been reversed. AI Core Revenue positioning remains at 94th/99th percentile (12m/LT) despite selling. Semis vs Software skew: Semis L/S ratio at ~3.0x vs Software ~1x. L/S funds down -2.3% MTD but still up +7.2% YTD.

bullets.title: Technicals: NDX failed above June high; breadth deteriorated to 47% above 200-day
bullets.body: OPCO's Ari Wald warns of bullish fatigue: 10Y yields fell 30bps to 5.05% but equities failed to respond. NDX failed above June high; RTY broke below 200-day average and support at 2,800. Russell 3000 participation above 200-day average deteriorated from 70% to 47% in two months. SOX has been consolidating near lows for four months. Equal-weight S&P outpaced cap-weighted by 225bp in the week—largest since Nov 2020—signaling defensive rotation.

bullets.title: Broad sector rotation: defensive outperformance, semis/growth lagging
bullets.body: Healthcare was upgraded to Overweight by OPCO (Ari Wald), payment processing (V/MA) upgraded, and banks downgraded. GS Prime reports Healthcare was net bought at the fastest pace in 7 months. Consumer Staples (XLP) outperformed by ~760bps over two weeks. Insurance Brokers, Info Services, P&C Insurance, and Payments benefited from AI unwind per UBS. Utilities and energy leading while software/cyber lag within tech.

bullets.title: Oil at new highs targeting $120; geopolitical risk elevated in Middle East
bullets.body: WTI/Brent Dec 2026 contracts hit new highs with analysts targeting $120. Flows out of the Gulf of Oman fell to 13.5 Mb/d from a 17 Mb/d early-October peak amid escalating Houthi strikes on Saudi infrastructure. Two ships sunk in the Strait of Hormuz. The gold-to-oil ratio at 42x vs. a 6-decade average of 20x suggests significant mean-reversion potential favoring oil.

bullets.title: Memory sector down 18-22% from peaks; CXMT 4F² DRAM claimed as competitive threat
bullets.body: The memory index is down 22% over 8 consecutive sessions and 45% from its June 2026 peak, with DRAM down 18.8% on the week. China's CXMT claimed a 4F² DRAM architecture breakthrough ~2 years ahead of Samsung's 2028 roadmap, spooking the sector. Jefferies and most analysts remain skeptical on commercialization timelines (mass-production unproven, yields uncertain), but equipment order ramps from TEL, Kokusai, and Daifuku signal real capex activity. NVIDIA also reportedly reduced HBM specs for Rubin Ultra, potentially easing tightness in 2-3 quarters.

bullets.title: Q3 earnings tracking +29% EPS growth; 84% beat rate above 1Y/5Y averages
bullets.body: S&P 500 Q3 blended EPS growth is tracking at 29.0-29.6% YoY with 84% of reporting companies beating consensus—above the 82% one-year and 78% five-year averages. Revenue beats at 67% are below the 77% one-year average. Earnings surprises at 2.6% above expectations, below the 13.8% one-year average. Key reporters next week: NFLX (Oct 20), META (Oct 21), TXN (Oct 21), T (Oct 21), CMCSA (Oct 22), SPOT (Oct 22), WDC (Oct 22).

bullets.title: AI financing questions: IMF flags $1.4T promised revenue vs $650B debt as systemic risk
bullets.body: The IMF flagged AI investment as a top financial stability risk due to circular financing structures—$1.4T in promised revenues backed by $650B in debt and $300B in equity. Gartner estimates data-center owners need $8.5T revenue through 2030 to cover capex and financing costs, vs only $3.6T projected enterprise/consumer AI revenue flowing to providers—leaving >$4T exposed to write-down risk. Both INTC and AVGO CEOs warned capital constraints may surpass compute constraints as the primary AI bottleneck.

bullets.title: Agentic AI threatens OTA commission pools; EXPE most at risk, ABNB upgraded
bullets.body: Hedgeye and Morgan Stanley both flagged that agentic AI tools (META Muse, Google AI Mode) now complete full travel bookings autonomously via browser automation, bypassing OTAs entirely. OTA stocks fell 15-25% YTD following Muse/Instinct launches. Hedgeye upgraded ABNB to Best Idea Long on hotel push strategy ($190-220 target) and keeps EXPE in short bias on B2B sustainability concerns. No major OTA has built systems allowing outside agents to complete bookings independently.

bullets.title: SpaceX 800MHz spectrum acquisition sparks telecom selloff; MS sees it as overdone
bullets.body: SpaceX acquired 800MHz low-band spectrum from Grain Management, causing AT&T, T-Mobile, and Verizon to lose ~$50B in combined market cap. Morgan Stanley reiterates OW on AT&T and T-Mobile, viewing the selloff as overdone and noting incumbents have 300-400MHz of low/mid-band spectrum across hundreds of thousands of sites—SpaceX needs significant infrastructure buildout to compete. MS estimates ~16M Starlink broadband subs by 2030 as incremental risk primarily to cable.

bullets.title: K-shaped economy: higher-income consumers strong, lower-income facing stress
bullets.body: Jefferies describes a 'K-shaped' economy with wealth gains concentrated in higher-income households while lower-income delinquencies and financial stress are rising. Bank earnings confirmed this: credit card spending from JPM/WFC/Citi running +10-11% YoY with resilient affluent spending, but ACI withdrew FY26 guidance on weakening core grocery comps driven by lower-income pressure. Retail sales overall beat at +6.8% YoY but fuel spend is back to 12% of total retail (near the 2022 high of 13%).

bullets.title: Midterm elections: Democratic sweep (55% probability) favors healthcare/defense spending
bullets.body: Piper Sandler assigns a 55% probability to a Democratic sweep and 15% to a Republican sweep. A Democratic sweep favors healthcare/non-defense spending and renewable energy; a Republican sweep favors defense, crypto, and AI. Morgan Stanley notes midterm results are unlikely to shift Trump's executive-led agenda (deregulation, tariffs). On average, S&P 500 returns +23% in the year following midterms with a Republican president and split Congress. 35+ data center ballot measures across 8 states on Nov 3 create near-term regulatory uncertainty for AI infrastructure.

bullets.title: Homebuilders flagged as AI-capex-decline hedge; housing drag could reverse
bullets.body: Multiple strategists (22V, OPCO) flag long homebuilders as a hedge against an AI capex slowdown: housing has not contributed to GDP for four years as AI spending and consumer drove above-trend growth. If AI capex declines sharply, the Fed would cut aggressively, yields would fall, and homebuilders historically perform best in that scenario. In early 2000s capex slowdowns, Household Products, Durables, and Food were leading sectors while Tech and Telecom were worst performers.
